messages:
alice: Heads-up — ran into a pretty opaque crash when trying to do a local eval run. CLI just dumps a stacktrace.
ben: ugh, stacktrace? can you paste the command + minimal config?
alice: command: `./scripts/eval-runner run --config configs/local/minimal.json`
The output is basically: `Traceback (most recent call last): File \"runner.py\", line 120, in <module> tasks = config['tasks'] KeyError: 'tasks'`
carla: that usually means we accept configs without any validation, so a missing top-level key triggers a raw exception. not great UX.
alice: exactly — i expected a friendly message like: "missing required field 'tasks' — run `eval-runner --validate <file>` for details". instead it's a full Python backtrace, which confuses product folks when they try local runs.
ben: agree. two quick fixes: (1) add a preflight config validation step with clear exit codes, (2) surface helpful hints + link to docs.
carla: i started a tiny schema draft last week. suggestion: use a small jsonschema and a `--validate`/`validate` subcommand that returns code 2 for user config errors. example schema snippet:```json
{
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["tasks"],
  "properties": {
    "tasks": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "object" } },
    "model": { "type": "string" }
  }
}
```
ben: +1. also add a short human-friendly error formatter so we show: "Config invalid: missing required property 'tasks' (see https://redwood.dev/docs/eval-harness/cli#config)".
david: @carla can you drop the schema in a small PR? i can add the CLI wiring and tests.
carla: will do. also noticed another related UX pain: relative paths in `dataset.path` break on mac when we run from the project root vs scripts dir. it's intermittent in CI.
alice: yes — local runs on mac produced `FileNotFoundError: ./data/test.json` while file was present. 
ben: likely cwd assumptions. we should normalize paths in the runner (Path(config.value).expanduser().resolve()) and write a test to run from a different cwd in CI.
carla: i'll include path normalization in the schema docs and add a tiny e2e that runs a minimal workload with cwd toggled.
ben: for CI: ensure the validator step is run in the pipeline before the heavy docker build. fail fast. add a `validate-config` job that runs quickly.
alice: perfect. can we also add a short `eval-runner validate <file>` output example in the docs? e.g.```bash
$ eval-runner validate configs/local/minimal.json
INVALID: missing required property 'tasks'
  at /configs/local/minimal.json:1
  hint: add a top-level \"tasks\" array. see https://redwood.dev/docs/eval-harness/cli#config
exit code: 2
```
carla: yeah i'll update the docs page and include the exit codes table.
eval-bot: CI job `eval-runner/validate` failed on branch carla/config-validator (2 new checks). <https://ci.redwood.dev/builds/4321|details> :warning:
ben: nice, incremental feedback loop. carla — want me to pair on the PR review? i can add the test harness and minimal fixture.
carla: please. i'll open PR in a bit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/pull/276 (WIP)
alice: thanks all. this should cut down the support noise — folks keep pasting scary traces instead of client-friendly messages. :pray:
ben: once merged i'll update the console docs and add a developer note in the repo README about local-run expectations.
carla: filing follow-ups: (1) add `--validate` subcommand, (2) path normalization, (3) CI validate job, (4) docs snippet + exit-code table, (5) unit + e2e tests.
david: noted. adding tasks to sprint board.
alice: cheers — i'll test the PR on my mac once it's ready and report back.
